Translation by the actual centroid uses an integer shift in the discrete coordinates and preserves the lattice and the mixed measure. Full affine span of ν means no affine hyperplane contains its support. Since the mean is zero, a zero positive directional moment would force that direction to vanish ν-almost everywhere. Directional moments are continuous on the unit sphere by bounded support, so their minimum m is positive. Also 0<m≤R and hence L≥G>0.

The hypograph construction gives a compact convex body. The cap t≥0 has mass Q and the body has mass LW+Q by integrating the thickness. The bounded and uniformly positive thickness L+g identifies positive extruded fibers exactly with positive section fibers. For each such base, take a section-fiber interior point and use strict vertical margins to see that t=0 cuts the extruded fiber properly.

Any closed ambient halfspace containing the mark contains a parallel closed halfspace through the mark. For a through-cap with positive t coefficient, subtracting the flat mass on each vertical segment gives the clipping formula: contribution above Q is −g(X) if ℓ<−g(X), ℓ in the middle, and L if ℓ>L. Replacing g by G in the negative clipping limit gives a lower bound.

For ℓ(X)=k v·X, if kR≤L, the positive integral is untruncated and dominates the truncated negative integral by zero mean. If kR>L, min(kx,L)≥Lx/R for x in [0,R], and the positive contribution is at least LWm/R≥GW, dominating the negative contribution. Equality holds at ℓ=0 for the flat cap.

For a negative t coefficient, the cap contains the lower segment over every base point X with ℓ(X)≥0. For a zero t coefficient it contains the entire vertical interval over the same closed region. For nonzero ℓ, the positive moment gives ν{ℓ≥0}≥Wm/R, and either cap has at least GW≥Q. The remaining horizontal downward cap has mass LW≥Q. Thus the infimum over all ambient directions, including purely integer normals, is exactly Q.

The theorem quantifies over the stated class of D and all continuous positive concave g with the stated lower bound on L. It prescribes one actual centroid mark and makes no assertion of maximizing depth over all sampled points.
